quality_flags.detail: [goal_mainflow_alignment] The goal statement lists three distinct outcomes: distinguishing exercise-involved live tracks from other live tracks, resolving Environment/Category differences, and determining Track Number continuity when an entity type changes. Main flow covers E/C conflict priority (step 4), Exercise Indicator conflict priority (step 5), and ID-conflict-driven correlation resolution (steps 6-8), but no main_flow step determines Track Number continuity when an entity type changes. The goal is therefore broader than the main flow and appears to conflate multiple use cases/actions into one goal. (atomic grounding: candidate remains incomplete (C2 JU as the acting stakeholder is not supported by the cited evidence cards.))

[mainflow_trigger_continuity] The Trigger is a set of operator/C2 JU actions (E/C change, difference-report rejection, auto-accept of E/C/ID/Exercise Indicator changes), but Main Flow step 1 restarts from the Precondition state - recognizing that two tracks are eligible for correlation and initiating dual-designation resolution. None of the Trigger variants is actually continued by step 1, so the main flow reads as a different scenario. (atomic grounding: candidate remains incomplete (No cited evidence supports the added detail that a C2 JU resolves the resulting identity classification conflict.))

[mainflow_trigger_continuity] The Trigger claim lists only Environment/Category change, difference-report rejection, and track-report auto-accept as initiators. Main Flow step 1 additionally enters the use case when the C2 JU recognizes that two reported tracks are eligible for correlation and when it receives a J7.2 message with Response Value field set to 3. These are distinct trigger events in the main flow but are absent from the Trigger slot, so the main flow does not continue from a complete and accurate trigger definition.
